newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power up ahead of cooler temps, outage.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power up ahead of cooler temps, outage.

text.p: Spot bulk power prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were trading higher Wednesday on forecasts of some cooler temperatures and a nuclear outage to begin later this week, sources said.

ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Wednesday was said to have traded at $22.50-23.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) from talk at $20.00-22.00 on Monday for Tuesday delivery, the brokers and marketers said.
Non-firm on peak power for Wednesday delivery was notionally pegged higher at $20.00-22.00 from a notional assessment at $18.00-20.00 on Monday.

Firm off-peak Wednesday ERCOT deliveries were pegged higher at $13.00-14.00 from $11.00-13.00 on Monday, while non firm off peak power was pegged at $11.00-13.00 from $9.00-11.00 on Monday, the sources said.
ERCOT peak power for the five business days of next week was said to be talked at $21.00-22.00 per MWh.

March ERCOT peak power was assessed higher at $21.00-21.50 after unconfirmed reports of morning trades at $20.75, from Monday talk at $20.00-20.50, while July/August peak power was said to be talked at $24.95-25.25 from a trade at $24.80 on Monday, the sources said.

Temperatures in Texas were expected to cool to just below normal for the end of the week, while the six to 10 day outlook called for temperatures to be one to five degrees below normal in northern sections and near normal through the rest of the state.
Also, Houston Lighting and Power's 1,250 megawatt South Texas unit 2 was expected to shut down for planned refueling and maintenance on Feb 7 for a scheduled 35 days.
